newsitem.title: GERMANY: Varta plans to resume dividend for 1997.
newsitem.headline: Varta plans to resume dividend for 1997.

text.p: German battery-maker Varta AG said on Monday it expected to resume dividend payments on its 1997 results for the first time since 1992.
The company said in a statement: "As a result of the developments in the first half of the year an appropriate dividend can be expected for 1997."
Predicting markedly improved results for 1997, it added, "The management board is confident that the favourable results developments at Varta will continue in the next few years."
Varta, which reported a loss of 25 million marks in 1996 on sales of 1.99 billion marks, said it would continue to streamline its organisation to make it more competitive.
In 1995, it reported sales of 2.01 million marks and a loss of 89 billion marks. It last paid a dividend of 10 marks in 1992.

Varta also announced the departure from its management board of its management board chairman Erhard Schipporeit on September 30. Schipporeit was departing to take up a post in the board of another company, it said without giving details.
Schipporeit's responsibilities would be shared between Varta's two other board members -- Wout van der Kooij and Georg Prilhofer -- for the time being.
